Known TE sequences are fed into RepeatMasker
Which are used to find intervals with TE homology

nodes.family: "PP Editorial New", "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif

runs.text: One of these unannotated families was MADE1/MADE2
It’s a short, 80 bp family composed of two palindromic repeats
RepeatMasker’s search found 71 loci without annotation
But a more sensitive BLAST search brought the count up to 378
To ensure these loci were genuine, various tests were used
Shuffling the sequence 500 times and BLASTing it against the reference sequence
Comparing orthologous positions in primates
Querying against profile hidden Markov models
These tests confirmed all but one locus

Standard consensus sequences encode a position’s most common base, pHMMs encode all base probabilities

panels.question: Why did you find known TEs if you had already masked these regions?

nodes.text: Dfam families were searched against the real genome and a synthetic one
Any hit in the synthetic genome must be a false positive
Bitscores of the hits from both searches
The bitscore cutoff is raised until only 0.2% of hits above it are false
RepeatModeler outputs a consensus sequence for each family it discovers
These family sequences are fed into RepeatMasker
RepeatMasker searches the genome for copies of each family
Each copy found is labelled with its family: the reannotation

nodes.text: Each TE copy has coordinates in the human genome
liftOver uses a chain file: blocks of whole-genome alignment between two species
The copy's coordinates are projected through its aligned block
The chimpanzee carries a copy at the orthologous position
Copies that fall in an alignment gap can't be lifted over
